headline: Medium risk: shared network/MCP and file-upload surfaces create leakage and workflow-conflict paths; no direct prompt-injection bridge is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack can call MCP servers and REST APIs, while Plane exposes file uploads and issue/task content. That creates a plausible manual or indirect content bridge, but no documented default parser-to-parser injection path is shown. Plane is not browser-based here, so the interaction is weaker than a shared filesystem or raw web-content parser.
conditions: IF Haystack ingests Plane-uploaded text as instructions without sanitization
IF an operator copies Plane content into an MCP tool call that Haystack executes
mitigations: Disable MCP endpoints that accept untrusted text
Add a strict instruction/data delimiter in Haystack prompts
Require manual review before copying Plane content into Haystack
Use separate workspaces for each agent
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all cross-agent content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and can call MCP/REST APIs; Plane handles files, images, notes, and issue/task data. Even without a shared filesystem, the pair can move sensitive work artifacts from Plane into Haystack outputs or external services in default-possible workflows, so leakage is plausible and not fully mitigated by the profiles.
conditions: IF Plane file uploads contain sensitive project data
IF Haystack forwards retrieved content to a third-party API or logs it externally
mitigations: Restrict Plane uploads to non-sensitive files
Turn off external egress in Haystack where possible
Redact files before retrieval into Haystack
Separate credentials and API keys per agent
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on cross-agent transfers

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plane explicitly does not write the filesystem and supports multiple instances, while Haystack exposes network/MCP access but no filesystem write is listed. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; the main overlap is read/egress and API use, which is a smaller coordination risk than mutable shared-state contention.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to mutate the same external API resource through MCP or REST
IF an orchestrator maps both agents onto the same mutable workspace despite Plane's no-write profile
mitigations: Assign separate API tokens per agent
Avoid shared mutable resources
Serialize any shared external writes
Document ownership of each workspace
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is a search-RAG agent that can surface retrieved content, and Plane is an issue/task system that can consume files and notes. If Plane treats Haystack output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect tasks or scheduling decisions. The profiles do not show verification gates, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Plane imports Haystack-generated text into issues or tasks without human verification
IF Haystack retrieves stale or hallucinated content that Plane then operationalizes
mitigations: Require human approval before creating Plane tasks from Haystack output
Attach source links to every Haystack-derived claim
Use a verification checklist in Plane
Limit Haystack to retrieval-only summaries
requires-engineering: add confidence scoring before task creation

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with Haystack touching anonymous usage statistics and Plane touching issues, tasks, files, and notes. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so only a limited compliance gap is visible: Plane's broader data classes could exceed Haystack's narrower telemetry scope if sensitive project data is routed through the pair.
conditions: IF Plane stores regulated or confidential content in files or notes
IF Haystack processes that content outside the operator's required retention policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Plane uploads
Set short retention on both systems
Review logging settings for both agents
Use separate environments for sensitive projects
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
